what: What is stopping us, in plain words. Hand-written because a machine cannot say who is waiting on whom. A blocker that clears is DELETED, not marked done.

blockers.what: The test is the only thing left
blockers.why: Every free improvement is done — the shortlist's corrections, what the AI is told about the company, and how the write-up talks about money. The last two cannot show up in our free test at all, because that test runs without the AI in it. That is exactly why they were done first, and it is why the number below barely moved. One paid run is now the only way to see whether any of it worked.
blockers.ask: About 15 euros, one run. Say go.

blockers.what: One deployment, and it now unblocks two things
blockers.why: The pipeline container is 316 commits behind and its safety check has never once published a result. It turns out this is not one item but the gate on another: every route to the master copy of our data begins by waking that container, so the 3,400 missing rules cannot be reconciled until it is redeployed. Two queue items, one decision.
blockers.ask: Read AWAITING_APPROVAL §13 and §14 — they are the same decision. No money.
